title: Peter Freed, Herod Struck Down
overview: King Herod kills the apostle James and jails Peter, but Peter is led out of prison by an angel, and Herod himself soon dies after accepting praise as a god.

parts.label: Herod turns on the church (vv. 1-5)
parts.note: This Herod is Herod Agrippa I, grandson of the Herod in the Christmas story, and he killed James, one of Jesus' three closest friends. Seeing this won him favor with some in Jerusalem, he jailed Peter under a heavy guard during the Passover festival, planning a public trial once the holy days were over.

parts.label: Walking out of prison (vv. 6-11)
parts.note: On the night before his trial, Peter is asleep, chained to a soldier on each side, when an angel wakes him, the chains drop, and the gates open. Peter thinks he is dreaming until he is standing alone in the street and realizes he really has been rescued.

parts.label: Knocking at Mary's door (vv. 12-17)
parts.note: Peter goes to the home of Mary, mother of John Mark, where people are praying for him, but the servant Rhoda is so excited she forgets to open the door, and no one believes her. Their guess that it is "his angel" reflects a belief of the time in a personal guardian spirit, and the James Peter names is probably Jesus' brother, who later led the Jerusalem church.

parts.label: Herod punishes the guards (vv. 18-19)
parts.note: At dawn Peter is gone, and Herod has the guards put to death. Guards who let a prisoner escape could face the penalty meant for that prisoner.

parts.label: Herod's death (vv. 20-23)
parts.note: The cities of Tyre and Sidon depended on Herod's lands for food, so they sought peace, and when the crowd hailed his speech as the voice of a god, he accepted it and was struck down. The Jewish historian Josephus also tells of Herod falling suddenly and fatally ill at Caesarea after being praised as divine, around AD 44.

parts.label: The message keeps growing (vv. 24-25)
parts.note: The king who tried to crush the movement is dead, yet the message about Jesus keeps spreading. Barnabas and Saul (later called Paul) finish the famine relief trip begun in the previous chapter and take John Mark with them.

think: James was killed and Peter walked free from the same prison system; how do you make sense of stories where one person is spared and another is not?
